content: Systematizing the monitoring process is crucial for effectiveness. This involves creating a structured workflow where specific individuals are responsible for scanning designated sources daily or weekly. A central database or CRM system should be used to log these demand signals, categorizing them by sector, potential project value, required crane capacity, and timeline. For each signal, key information should be captured, including the ultimate client (e.g., the mine or developer), the principal contractor, project location, and key contact persons if available. Furthermore, demonstrating a certified quality management system (ISO 9001) and an occupational health and safety management system (ISO 45001) is increasingly becoming a prerequisite for pre-qualification, especially for major clients in the mining and energy sectors. For equipment, every crane and piece of lifting tackle (e.g., slings, shackles, spreader beams) must have a valid certificate of test and examination. For cranes, this involves an annual load test and inspection conducted by a Lifting Machinery Inspector (LMI). An LMI is an individual deemed competent and registered by the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) to carry out such inspections. A crane without a valid, in-date load test certificate is illegal to operate.
